Old fashioned phones lack many of the vulnerabilities of modern smart phones, but there are two key points to remember.

1) Because the phone always has to be able to make and receive phone calls, it always has to keep announcing its position to every cell phone tower within radio range. An old fashioned phone probably could keep quiet if you took its battery out, but I would also put it in a Faraday cage.

2) The NSA has been influencing all chip makers for decades, and even an old cell phone may have backdoors. If you're just hiding from drug cartels or Yakuza, you probably don't need to worry. If you want to hide from the NSA, you're kind of hosed, because even if you lock down your phone, they have multiple ways of finding you.
Do you think carrying the phone in a foil pouch would make any difference?

A foil pouch is a Faraday cage. It should block all electromagnetic waves. Super-sneaky spies can probably use sonic waves in an attempt to infer stuff about your phone, but even if sound waves are a vulnerability, most foil pouches should muffle them. If you power down the phone and put it in a pouch, it should be pretty hard to eavesdrop on. (Modern smartphones probably have backdoors to power them back up without warning, but if it is inside the pouch, you shouldn't be bothered by that until you get to a supposedly safe location and take out your phone, only to be surprised that it powered up without you.)
